features.text: The patient has been experiencing lower back pain since Saturday morning.
The patient believes he strained his lower back while helping his daughter lift heavy boxes.
The patient felt something pop in his lower back and had to lie down for a while before the pain eased.
The patient's lower back has been stiff since the onset of the pain.
The patient has a history of type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and osteoarthritis in his knee.
The patient's back pain is located in the lower back and has an intensity of 6 or 7 out of 10.
The patient initially felt tingling in his right toe, but it has since resolved.
The patient's back pain is worse when moving or sitting for long periods, but lying on his right side helps a little.
The patient has not experienced bowel or bladder dysfunction, fever, or significant neurological deficits such as numbness, weakness, or loss of reflexes since the onset of his back pain.
The patient does not have any numbness or weakness in his legs, and the tingling in his right toe has gone away.
The patient's lower back is tender, especially when bending or stretching, and it is pretty stiff.
The patient has tenderness in his lower back, right around the middle to lower part, and feels some muscle tightness there.
The patient has not undergone any imaging studies of the lumbar spine since the onset of his symptoms.
The patient has been managing his back pain with Tylenol, ibuprofen, and an icy heat pack, but it hasn't helped much.
The patient has not noticed any changes in his bowel or bladder function since the onset of his back pain.
The patient has not experienced any numbness, tingling, or weakness in his legs since the onset of his lower back pain.
The patient has not experienced any recent trauma or falls that could have contributed to his lower back pain.
The patient has not had any recent imaging studies for his back.
